title: Recent Advances and Precision Measurements with the JYFLTRAP Double Penning Trap Mass Spectrometer
byline: Ge; Zhuang; Ambrosio-Macias; Natalia; Candiello; Anita; Chinthakayala; Saikumar; Eronen; Tommi; Jaries; Arthur; Kankainen; Anu; Karadimas; Angelos; Kootte; Bria
html:
Abstract:High-precision atomic-mass measurements with the JYFLTRAP double Penning-trap mass spectrometer at the IGISOL facility provide direct information on decay energies, nuclear binding and shell evolution, isomer excitation energies, and masses relevant to nuclear astrophysics. Recent work has combined the phase-imaging ion-cyclotron-resonance (PI-ICR) method with established ion-purification and selective ion-production techniques to study low-yield nuclei and resolve isomeric states. At JYFLTRAP/IGISOL, mass-selective buffer-gas cooling, Ramsey cleaning, resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS), phase-dependent cleaning, and species-resolved PI-ICR analysis are used in complementary combinations according to the ion yield and the required separation. Laser-frequency tagging correlates individual ion events with the corresponding laser frequency and enables state-resolved resonance-ionization spectra. Selected ion bunches are used for direct mass measurements with PI-ICR or time-of-flight ion-cyclotron resonance (TOF-ICR), for ion counting, or for post-trap decay spectroscopy. When multiple species or states are present, resolved PI-ICR phase spots allow the mass-measurement data to be assigned to the corresponding component. Examples from the recent program include high-precision $Q$-value measurements, neutron-deficient nuclei below $^{100}$Sn, neutron-rich fission fragments, rapid structural evolution around $N\approx60$, and rare-earth nuclei relevant to the astrophysical $r$ process.
